context.endUser: An Instagram creator or small business owner who gets many comments and wants to answer them with a DM automatically. Knows Instagram well, has never set up an API.
context.product: Sends a DM to people who comment a keyword on your Instagram posts.

coreJobs.name: Create an automation that sends a DM when someone comments a keyword
coreJobs.momentOfValue: A DM goes out, or a test DM arrives on the creator's own account

coreJobs.name: See who received a DM and from which keyword
coreJobs.momentOfValue: A list of people reached by an automation

assumptions: The product's purpose was inferred from its name and the landing copy, since no screen states it.
The app runs without a backend, so every API call fails. The review judges what the interface tells the person when that happens.
The creator has an Instagram business account but no Meta developer account.

fiveSecondTest.whatIsThis: Some AI tool for Instagram. The headline says supercharge and automation, not what it does.
fiveSecondTest.whoIsItFor: Creators, from the line about 10,000+ creators.
fiveSecondTest.whatToDo: Get Started or Learn More, without saying what either leads to.
fiveSecondTest.note: Nothing in the first view mentions comments, keywords or DMs.

steps.action: Read the landing page and clicked Get Started
steps.observation: It opened a dashboard, not a way to create an automation.

steps.action: Clicked Create Flow under Quick Actions
steps.observation: Nothing happened. The URL stayed on /dashboard and no dialog opened.
The table says No data and nothing explains what a flow is.

steps.action: Clicked Create Flow in the top-right corner
steps.observation: A modal opened with nine fields and a greyed-out Submit button that gives no reason.

steps.action: Filled six fields, picking COMMENT_KEYWORD and page_1784140 from the lists
steps.observation: Submit turned on only after a delay in seconds and an account shown as a raw page id were filled in.

steps.action: Clicked Submit and confirmed 'Are you sure you want to create this flow?'
steps.observation: A bouncing Success! toast appeared and the modal closed.
The row says ACTIVE although no Instagram account is connected, and there is no way to preview or test the DM.
It asks for a Graph API access token, a webhook verify token, an app secret and a Facebook page id.

journeys.note: Stopped at Settings. A creator without a Meta developer account cannot go further, and nothing can be tested before that step.

cuts.note: Name it after the keyword, such as LINK on any post. It can be renamed under More options.
Comment keyword is the only trigger that works today.
The name and the message already say what the automation does.
Use the connected account, and ask only when there is more than one.
Nothing in the app uses tags.
New automations start on, and the list can pause them.
One keyword, with a hint that a single word works best.
With a live preview of the DM next to it.

steps.observation: Cards show John Doe, Jane Smith and Mike Johnson with stock avatars before any automation has run.

steps.action: Clicked the unlabeled eye icon on a card
steps.observation: A modal lists contact_status SUBSCRIBED, tags and last_seen. Nothing says which DM or keyword reached the person.
Nothing happened on screen. The click only logged 'export contacts' to the console.

journeys.note: The list is sample data, so it cannot tell the creator who received a DM.

tells.note: 12,345 contacts and +12.5% trends on an account with no automations.
Nine top-level items that mirror the data model.
Triggers, Broadcasts, Templates, Analytics and Integrations sit in the menu, all marked Coming soon.
Trigger type, account, delay and status each have one sensible answer, and the form still asks for all four.
Create Flow sits at x 1257 to 1408, y 80. The empty table spans x 312 to 1384, y 302 to 450.
Three gradient buttons compete in Quick Actions, and two on the landing page.
Delete removes the row at once, with no undo.
Submit sits bottom left in the modal; Save Changes sits top right in Settings.
Row and card icon buttons measure 22 by 22 pixels.
The interface is consistently in English.

findings.title: Going live needs developer credentials a creator does not have

evidence.observation: Connecting Instagram asks for a Graph API access token, a webhook verify token, an app secret and a Facebook page id.
The create form requires an Instagram account, offered only as the raw id page_1784140.

findings.why: The people this product is for have an Instagram account, not a Meta developer app. They stop at this screen, and nothing lets them see an automation work before it.
findings.fix: Let people build and preview an automation first, and send a test to their own account. Ask to connect Instagram when they save, with a Sign in with Instagram button instead of token fields.

findings.title: The app opens on a sales page, then on invented numbers

evidence.observation: The root route is a landing page whose headline says 'Supercharge your Instagram with AI-powered automation' and never mentions comments or DMs.
Get Started leads to a dashboard showing 12,345 contacts, 48,392 messages and +12.5% trends for an account with no automations.
The dashboard numbers are hardcoded.

findings.why: A new user never sees what the product does or where to start. The fake numbers also make it hard to trust any real ones later.
findings.principle: Match between the system and the real world (Nielsen)
findings.fix: Open the app on Automations. For a new account, show one sentence on what an automation does and a button to create the first one. Show numbers only when they are real.

findings.title: Nine fields in a modal before the first automation

evidence.observation: Create Flow opens a modal with nine fields: name, trigger type, description, keywords, account, message, delay, tags and status.
Submit stays greyed out until six of them are filled, including a delay in seconds, and nothing says which are missing.
The button is disabled={!isValid} with no message.

findings.why: A working automation needs a keyword and a message. The other fields slow people down, the trigger and status options are code words, and there is no preview of the DM they are writing.
findings.fix: Move creation to its own page. Ask for the keyword and the message in one sentence, show a live preview of the DM, give the rest defaults under More options, and validate on save with specific messages.
findings.code: <label htmlFor="keyword">When someone comments</label> <input id="keyword" /> on any post, send them this DM: <textarea id="message" />

findings.title: The empty list says No data, with the Create button far away

evidence.observation: The empty table reads 'No data' in the middle of the page. Create Flow sits in the top-right corner, about 550 pixels from that text.
The empty state is the words No data in light gray.

findings.why: The empty list is the moment a new user needs to be told what a flow is and how to make one. The screen gives neither, and the only action is outside the content.
findings.fix: Replace No data with a short explanation and put the create button inside the empty state. Keep a New automation button next to the list title once there are items.

findings.title: Success! appears even when nothing worked

evidence.observation: Save Changes showed a Success! toast while the request to /api/instagram/connect returned 404.
After creating a flow the toast says Success! and the row says ACTIVE, with no Instagram account connected and nothing pointing to the next step.
Errors are caught and only logged to the console.

findings.why: People believe their automation is working when it cannot send anything. They find out only when followers complain that no DM arrived.
findings.fix: Check the response and show a specific error when a request fails. After creating an automation, open its page and say whether it is live, what is missing, and offer a test.
findings.code:
const response = await fetch(url, options);
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Instagram answered ${response.status}`);

findings.title: Half the navigation leads to Coming soon

evidence.observation: The sidebar has nine items. Triggers, Broadcasts, Templates, Analytics and Integrations are marked Coming soon.
Each of those opens a page that says it is coming soon, with a Notify Me button that does nothing.
Quick Actions: Send Broadcast shows an alert saying Coming soon and View Analytics does nothing.

findings.why: Every dead item costs a click and makes the product feel unfinished. The five tables at the top level also hide the one job people came to do.
findings.fix: Keep four items that match jobs: Automations, Activity, Contacts and Settings. Remove what is not built, and fold triggers and templates into the automation page.

findings.title: Row actions are invisible, unlabeled, and delete has no undo

evidence.observation: Edit, copy and delete appear only on hover, as 22 by 22 pixel icons without labels or accessible names.
Delete removed the flow at once and left 'No data', with no undo.
Edit only logs to the console and copy has an empty handler.

findings.why: On a phone the actions never appear. On a computer people have to guess what each icon does, and one slip deletes an automation for good.
findings.fix: Show an Edit link on every row and put Pause and Delete in a labeled More menu. After delete, show 'Deleted. Undo' for a few seconds.

findings.title: The app does not fit on a phone

evidence.observation: At 390 pixels the page needs 1,213 pixels of width, so the browser zooms out until the text is too small to read.
The main area has ml-64 and min-w-[900px], and the sidebar is always fixed.

findings.why: Creators check comments on their phone. On a phone, this app is unusable.
findings.fix: Collapse the sidebar into a top bar below the md breakpoint, remove fixed widths, and stack grids into one column on small screens.

findings.title: Gray text below the contrast minimum on every screen

evidence.observation: 14 of 33 text elements on the landing page are below 4.5 to 1, such as #99a1af on white at 2.6 to 1.
21 of 54 text elements on the dashboard fail the same check.

findings.why: Descriptions, dates and labels are hard to read, especially on a phone outdoors.
findings.fix: Use gray-600 or darker for secondary text on white.

findings.title: Keyboard focus is invisible

evidence.observation: With keyboard focus on the Flow Name field, the computed outline style is none and there is no box shadow.
button:focus sets outline to none, and inputs use outline-none.

findings.why: People who use the keyboard cannot see where they are in the form.
findings.fix: Remove outline: none and add a focus-visible ring in the brand color.

findings.title: Copy that could belong to any product, and made-up proof

evidence.observation: 'Streamline your workflow and engage your audience seamlessly. The all-in-one platform...', 'Trusted by 10,000+ creators', and testimonials from 'Sarah Johnson, CEO at TechCorp'.
'Welcome back, John!' and a Recent Activity list of John Doe and Jane Smith with stock avatars.

findings.why: The words do not say what the product does, and invented proof damages trust once someone notices it.
findings.fix: Say the job plainly: 'Send a DM to everyone who comments a keyword on your posts.' Remove the testimonials, the user counts and the placeholder people until there are real ones.

findings.title: The look is a stock generated template

evidence.observation: 7 gradient elements, 2 gradient headlines, 3 blurred layers and 8 large rounded shadowed boxes on the landing page.
Every card scales on hover, every icon sits in a pale purple square, and emoji decorate the headings.

findings.why: Nothing on screen reflects this product or its audience, and the decoration competes with the few things that matter.
findings.fix: Pick one brand color for the main action, use solid surfaces and plain borders, left-align text, drop emoji and sparkle icons, and keep motion for feedback.
